messages:
customer-jdoe: Hi team — our private inference traffic to model.redwood-inference.internal:443 started failing intermittently yesterday. App streams hit ECONNRESET during TLS handshake. No config changes on our side. Can you help triage?

maria-support: Sorry you're hitting this — we'll take a look. Quick Q: is this a VPC Private deployment or Dedicated? And are the inference workers in a private subnet behind a NAT?

customer-jdoe: Private (VPC) deployment, workers in private subnets routed through a NAT gateway. We see the failures from multiple instances, not just one.

ben-netops: @maria-support @customer-jdoe can you grab a tcpdump from one of the affected hosts when it reproduces? e.g.:
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host model.redwood-inference.internal and port 443 -w /tmp/inf_tls.pcap
```
Also please paste the instance's subnet ID and the NACL ID if possible.

customer-jdoe: Captured a small pcap. Subnet: subnet-0a1b2c3d. NACL: acl-07e9f8ab. Attaching shortly.

julia-engr: If you can also run an openssl client to reproduce the handshake, that helps isolate TLS vs network drop:
```
openssl s_client -connect model.redwood-inference.internal:443 -servername model.redwood-inference.internal -tlsextdebug
```
What error do you see from openssl?

customer-jdoe: openssl shows: "TLS handshake failure" and then socket: Connection reset by peer. cURL sometimes returns "Empty reply from server" and sometimes instant RST.

maria-support: Thanks — two quick suspects: 1) NACL is stateless so ephemeral return ports need explicit allow, 2) a middlebox (NAT/NVA) doing TLS-inspection/DPIs terminating or dropping sessions. Ben, can you check the NACL rules and flow logs?

ben-netops: I pulled the NACL (acl-07e9f8ab). It currently has explicit ALLOW for 443 outbound, but there is a DENY rule blocking 1024-65535 outbound. Because NACLs are stateless, return traffic on ephemeral ports will be dropped. That matches RSTs during handshake.

customer-jdoe: Oh wow — we recently hardened the NACLs with a deny block for ephemeral range. Is that the typical cause?

julia-engr: Yes — for TCP connections initiated from your hosts to external 443, the remote server responds from port 443 to a high ephemeral port on your host. With a stateless NACL that denies those high ports, the SYN/ACK or subsequent packets get dropped and the stack or a middlebox may reset.

maria-support: Concrete remediation options:
- Update the NACL to allow ephemeral return ports (1024-65535) both inbound and outbound, or at least allow ephemeral range inbound if outbound 443 is allowed. Example AWS CLI check:
```
aws ec2 describe-network-acls --network-acl-ids acl-07e9f8ab
```
And to add a broad allow (use with your change controls):
```
aws ec2 create-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-07e9f8ab --rule-number 100 --protocol tcp --rule-action allow --egress false --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --port-range From=1024,To=65535
```
- Alternatively, make the NACL symmetric: ensure any allow you add for outbound 443 is mirrored for inbound ephemeral ports.

ben-netops: Also check if your NAT gateway has any custom security appliance in path. If you have a packet-inspecting firewall, it might be closing TLS 1.3 handshakes it can't inspect. Quick conntrack check on the host (if using linux NAT boxes):
```
sudo conntrack -L | grep 443
```
If you see lots of SYN entries with no ESTABLISHED counterpart, that's a hint.

customer-jdoe: We do have a third-party firewall in front of the NAT (inline). We recently pushed a policy update last week. Could that coincide?

julia-engr: Possibly. Two-step approach: 1) Temporarily relax the NACL to allow ephemeral return ports and test. If that fixes it, then NACL was the root cause. 2) If problems persist, bypass the inline appliance (route around) for a test subnet or push a pass-through rule on the appliance for traffic to model.redwood-inference.internal to confirm.

customer-jdoe: I opened a change to allow ephemeral inbound (1024-65535) on the NACL and tested — openssl now completes the handshake consistently. Streaming sessions stable.

maria-support: Great news — looks like NACL was the culprit. For long-term, either keep symmetric rules or move to stateful SGs for host-level control and reserve NACLs for coarse grained filtering. Also document the inline appliance change if it was modified.

customer-jdoe: Will do. One follow-up: should we restrict ephemeral range to a smaller window instead of full 1024-65535?

julia-engr: You can pick a narrower ephemeral range on your hosts (sysctl net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range) and allow that range in the NACL. Example to check: `cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range`. Then update NACL to match that smaller range. That reduces exposure but remember to keep it symmetric.

maria-support: Closing loop — marking this resolved on our side. If you want, we can schedule a short runbook entry for your infra team to avoid future regressions. :thumbsup:

customer-jdoe: Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick help. We'll keep the NACL change and track the firewall policy.
